job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today I learned so much about staying safe online during our school workshop. I realized that using my pet’s name and birthday for my password is a huge mistake because such personal details are easy for others to guess. I also learned that using the same password for every account is dangerous; if one site gets hacked, all my accounts are at risk. My teacher emphasized that a bank will never call and ask for my OTP or PIN, even if they know my name or claim my account will be blocked. These callers are just scammers trying to steal money. Furthermore, I discovered that closing a browser tab does not automatically log me out of my accounts on a shared computer; I must manually click the sign-out button every time. Finally, we discussed cyberbullying. It is never okay to handle bullying alone or reply in anger. Instead, I should report it immediately, as online harassment is serious and can cause deep emotional harm, regardless of whether there is physical contact. I feel much more confident now about protecting my digital life and keeping my private information secure from those who wish to cause harm.

items.evidence: I realized that using my pet’s name and birthday for my password is a huge mistake because such personal details are easy for others to guess.
items.q: Why is a password made from a pet's name and birthday risky?
options: Other people can easily guess such details
Pets' names are found in common word lists
Birthdays are checked by the website itself
Short passwords are always blocked by sites
items.explain: Personal details like a pet's name and birthday are easy for others to guess.

wrong.why: picks a plausible technical-sounding reason not given in the passage
invents a website rule that the passage never mentions
thinks the problem is only password length

items.evidence: I also learned that using the same password for every account is dangerous; if one site gets hacked, all my accounts are at risk.
items.q: Meera uses one password everywhere. One small website gets hacked. What is the result?
options: Her other accounts are also at risk
Only that one website account is at risk
Her accounts stay safe if it is strong
Her other accounts are locked for safety
items.explain: With one shared password, a hack on one site puts all the accounts at risk.

wrong.why: thinks a hack affects only the site that was attacked
thinks one strong password protects every account
assumes accounts are automatically protected after a hack

items.evidence: My teacher emphasized that a bank will never call and ask for my OTP or PIN, even if they know my name or claim my account will be blocked.
items.q: A caller knows your name and says your account will be blocked. What does this show?
options: The caller is a scammer, not the bank
The caller is real because he knows you
The caller is real if you share a PIN
The caller is a bank worker in a hurry
items.explain: A bank never asks for an OTP or PIN, even if the caller knows your name.

wrong.why: thinks knowing the name proves the caller is genuine
thinks the PIN must be given to avoid blocking
excuses the pressure as normal bank behaviour

items.evidence: Furthermore, I discovered that closing a browser tab does not automatically log me out of my accounts on a shared computer; I must manually click the sign-out button every time.
items.q: Aman checks his email on a school computer and closes the tab. What may happen next?
options: The next user may open his email
His email is signed out automatically
His email is safe once the tab closes
The computer will ask for his password
items.explain: Closing a tab does not log you out, so the next person may open your account.

wrong.why: thinks closing the tab logs him out
thinks closing the tab makes the account safe
assumes the computer re-checks the password by itself
